title: Add durable local actor names
description: Add a local actor-name facility so an operator can start an exact configured actor with a human-readable name, for example: start teams::coder-1 as "Bob". The FQN remains the authoritative actor identity. After binding, operator and MCP clients must be able to resolve Bob to teams::coder-1 and use the exact FQN for lifecycle and directed-message operations. This is a local Teams capability, distinct from federation aliases. Names persist across actor stop, restart, and daemon restart. Implement the feature through the organization, MongoDB, operator HTTP, MCP, and tekroo CLI layers with deterministic validation and collision handling.
acceptance_criteria: tekroo supports the command form role teams::coder-1 start --as Bob and starts the exact actor while durably binding Bob
local names are trimmed, Unicode NFKC-normalized display strings of 1 through 64 Unicode code points; control characters are rejected and case-insensitive uniqueness uses Unicode case folding
each actor has at most one local name and each normalized local name identifies at most one actor within its team
binding the same normalized name to the same actor is idempotent; binding it to a different actor fails; supplying a different name for an already named actor requires an explicit rename

tekroo exposes role-name bind ACTOR NAME, role-name rename ACTOR NAME, role-name remove ACTOR, and role-name resolve TEAM NAME; MCP extends tekroo_roles_control with optional local_name for start and adds tekroo_actor_names with bind, rename, remove, and resolve operations
the MCP operator surface can start an exact actor with an optional local name and can resolve a local name to its exact FQN
local names are unique within a team under case-insensitive normalization while preserving the chosen display spelling
a local name remains bound to the same FQN across stop, restart, process replacement, and tekrood restart
durable lifecycle commands, organizational messages, task ownership, and evidence continue to use the exact actor FQN rather than the local name
renaming or removing a local name is explicit and cannot silently retarget queued or historical work
unknown names and collisions fail clearly without starting, stopping, messaging, or retargeting the wrong actor
role-name resolve TEAM NAME searches only that exact team; a same-spelled name in another team is not found rather than reported as a cross-team mismatch
role ACTOR start --as NAME on an already-running exact actor validates or creates the binding and returns idempotent success without restarting the actor
role-name remove ACTOR is idempotent when the actor has no local name and does not alter actor lifecycle state
role-name rename ACTOR NAME is idempotent for the same normalized name; an exact display-spelling match is a no-op and an explicit case-only rename updates the preserved display spelling
the 64-code-point limit is applied after trimming and Unicode NFKC normalization; empty and whitespace-only names are rejected
a local name that parses as an actor FQN or contains the FQN separator :: is rejected; no additional role-name reservation is required
the authenticated operator HTTP API exposes POST /v1/actor-names/bind, POST /v1/actor-names/rename, POST /v1/actor-names/remove, and GET /v1/actor-names/resolve with the same semantics as CLI and MCP
local names are never removed implicitly by lifecycle changes; removing a configured actor is outside this feature, and an existing binding is changed only by explicit rename or remove
binding or renaming an actor that is not exactly configured in the named team fails without persisting a binding or starting any actor
successful resolve returns actor_fqn, team, and display_name consistently through HTTP and MCP; the CLI prints that same JSON object
existing exact-FQN lifecycle and messaging behavior remains backward compatible when no local name is supplied
unit, MongoDB integration, HTTP, MCP, CLI, restart-persistence, collision, and negative-path tests pass
constraints: Do not edit accepted contract packages in place; create a successor contract only if the implementation truly requires a normative contract change
Do not reuse federation alias types or federation routing for local actor names
Do not make the local name an actor identity, authorization principal, message recipient identity, task owner identity, or execution identity
Do not start an actor merely because a name is resolved or a message is addressed through the intermediary
Do not migrate v3 data, alter SMA, deploy the result, or modify unrelated repository content
Keep the implementation small, deterministic, and idiomatic Go
